matched.matchReason: Both findings describe the identical vulnerability where the JWT middleware accepts both RS256 and HS256 algorithms in the algorithms array at lines 46-51 (expected) / line 54 (actual). Both identify that the public key can be used as an HMAC secret to forge tokens. Both describe the same attack scenario: fetching the public key from /.well-known/jwks.json, creating an HS256 token with admin role, and accessing /api/admin/flag. Both are critical severity vulnerabilities enabling complete authentication bypass.

extra.title: IDOR Vulnerability in /api/users Endpoint - Unauthorized User Enumeration and Admin Data Exposure
extra.assessment: New discovery - This is a legitimate vulnerability where authenticated users can enumerate all 76+ system users including admin accounts without proper authorization checks. The endpoint returns complete user records without role-based access control. This is a valid finding not in the expected list.

extra.title: Open Registration Without Email Verification - /api/auth/register
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability where the registration endpoint accepts arbitrary usernames, passwords, and emails without any email verification or approval process. Immediately issues valid RS256 JWT tokens with no rate limiting. This is a legitimate security issue enabling account enumeration and authentication bypass.

extra.title: User Enumeration via Registration Endpoint - Direct Username Confirmation
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability where the endpoint returns HTTP 409 with 'Username already exists' error, allowing attackers to enumerate valid usernames without authentication. This is a legitimate information disclosure vulnerability enabling user enumeration attacks.

extra.title: Input Validation Vulnerability - Type Confusion in Authentication Parameters
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability where the login endpoint accepts non-string values for the password parameter (boolean, numeric, array, objects) and returns different error responses (500 vs 401) based on data type. This indicates improper input validation and potential type confusion vulnerabilities.

extra.title: Unrestricted User Enumeration - /api/users Endpoint
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability where any authenticated user can enumerate all 108+ system users without restrictions. The endpoint returns complete user records with IDs, usernames, and roles for all users including admins, without implementing access control checks. Combined with open registration, this enables complete reconnaissance.

extra.title: IDOR - Horizontal Privilege Escalation via User Enumeration in /api/users
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid IDOR vulnerability allowing authenticated users to access information about other users through enumeration. The endpoint exposes 113+ user accounts including admin accounts without proper authorization checks, violating principle of least privilege.

extra.title: Public API Documentation Disclosure (Information Exposure)
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid vulnerability where complete API documentation is exposed at /api/docs without authentication. The endpoint returns the full list of all API endpoints, HTTP methods, request/response schemas, authentication mechanism details (RS256, JWKS URI), and indicates protected endpoints. Combined with public JWKS endpoint, this enables complete attack surface mapping.

extra.title: CORS Misconfiguration - Wildcard Allow-Origin Enables Information Disclosure
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid CORS misconfiguration where all endpoints return Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * headers, allowing any website to fetch sensitive API documentation and public keys via cross-origin requests. This enables reconnaissance and bypasses same-origin policy.

extra.title: CORS Misconfiguration - Access-Control-Allow-Origin Wildcard
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid CORS misconfiguration where the /api/auth/login endpoint returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * for all requests, allowing credential submission from any malicious website. This enables credential stuffing attacks and phishing via cross-origin POST requests.

extra.title: JKU Header SSRF Vulnerability in JWT Processing
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid SSRF vulnerability where the JWT validation endpoint processes the 'jku' (JSON Key URL) header without proper validation and attempts to fetch keys from arbitrary URLs. Different response codes (401 vs 400) indicate the application attempts to fetch from attacker-specified URLs, enabling SSRF attacks to scan internal services and potentially perform key injection.
